title.en: Short-term sources: trade credit, factoring, lease, commercial paper and ICDs

objectives.en: Explain commercial paper and inter-corporate deposits

narration.en: A kirana store gets rice from the wholesaler today and pays after a month. That simple promise is one of the biggest sources of business finance.
narration.kn: ಕಿರಾಣಿ ಅಂಗಡಿ ಇಂದು ಸಗಟು ವ್ಯಾಪಾರಿಯಿಂದ ಅಕ್ಕಿ ಪಡೆದು ಒಂದು ತಿಂಗಳ ನಂತರ ಪಾವತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಸರಳ ಭರವಸೆಯೇ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಹಣಕಾಸಿನ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಮೂಲಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು.

body.en: Trade credit is the credit extended by one trader to another when buying goods; it appears as sundry creditors or accounts payable. It is a convenient, continuous, short-term source that needs no charge on assets. Factoring is a financial service in which a factor, usually a bank or specialised firm, discounts the bills or buys the receivables of a business, collects the debts, and gives information about the creditworthiness of customers. Factoring may be with recourse (the business bears bad debts) or without recourse (the factor bears them).
body.kn: ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ಸಾಲ ಎಂದರೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆದಾರರ ಸಾಲ. ಫ್ಯಾಕ್ಟರಿಂಗ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಫ್ಯಾಕ್ಟರ್ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಖರೀದಿಸಿ ಹಣ ವಸೂಲಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Trade credit is credit from suppliers. In factoring, a factor buys the firm's receivables and collects the money.
narration.kn: ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ಸಾಲ ಎಂದರೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆದಾರರ ಸಾಲ. ಫ್ಯಾಕ್ಟರಿಂಗ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಫ್ಯಾಕ್ಟರ್ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಖರೀದಿಸಿ ಹಣ ವಸೂಲಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Trade credit: the supplier gives goods today and the buyer pays later, say in sixty days.

say.en: Trade credit: the supplier gives goods today and the buyer pays later, say in sixty days.
Factoring: the factor buys the firm's receivables, pays cash now and collects from customers. With recourse, the firm bears bad debts.

text.en: With recourse: firm bears bad debts

say.en: Lease: the lessor owns the asset; the lessee uses it and pays lease rent.
Commercial paper is an unsecured promissory note of a well-rated company. Inter-corporate deposits are short-term deposits between companies.

narration.en: Match each short-term source to the situation.

prompt.en: Match each short-term source to the situation.

explanation.en: Short-term sources meet working-capital needs: credit from suppliers, cash for receivables, use of assets without buying them, and unsecured borrowing by strong companies.

right.en: A supplier lets a retailer pay for goods in 60 days
A bank buys a firm's receivables and collects them
The factor, not the firm, bears any bad debts
A hospital uses an MRI machine for monthly rentals; ownership stays with the lessor
A highly rated company issues an unsecured promissory note for 90 days
One company places its surplus funds with another for three months

body.en: Lease financing: the owner of an asset (lessor) lets another party (lessee) use it in return for periodic lease rentals; ownership stays with the lessor. It lets a firm use machinery without a large investment. Commercial paper (CP) is an unsecured promissory note issued by firms with a good credit rating to raise short-term funds, usually cheaper than a bank loan. Inter-corporate deposits (ICDs) are unsecured short-term deposits placed by one company with another.
body.kn: ಗುತ್ತಿಗೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ ಆಸ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಒಡೆತನವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಪತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಅಂತರ-ಕಾರ್ಪೊರೇಟ್ ಠೇವಣಿಗಳು ತ್ವರಿತ, ಭದ್ರತೆರಹಿತ ಅಲ್ಪಾವಧಿ ನಿಧಿಗಳು.

points.en: Lessor owns; lessee uses and pays rent

narration.en: With a lease, the firm uses an asset without owning it. Commercial paper and inter-corporate deposits are quick, unsecured short-term funds.

title.en: Cost of skipping a cash discount

caption.en: Terms "2/10, net 30" mean 2% off if paid in 10 days, else full price in 30 days. Skipping the discount is a costly loan.

narration.en: Move the discount and the credit days and see what trade credit really costs when the discount is skipped.

tryThis.en: Check that 2/10, net 30 costs about 37% a year.
Stretch the credit period to 60 days. What happens to the cost?
If a bank lends at 12%, should the buyer borrow to take the discount?

problem.en: A garment exporter has ₹50 lakh of receivables due in 90 days. A factor offers to pay 85% now and the rest on collection, without recourse. Explain what the exporter gains and who bears bad debts.

steps.en: The remaining ₹7.5 lakh (less the factor's fees) comes after collection.
The factor collects from buyers, saving the exporter collection effort.
Since it is without recourse, the factor bears any bad debts.

answer.en: ₹42.5 lakh of immediate cash, freedom from collection work, and no bad-debt risk for the exporter.
